title: Why You're Looking for Safety (Not Confidence)

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们除了用时间换取金钱，还能赚到更多的钱，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个激动人心的好消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·福特的“一对多”项目现在已经开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，比如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于2022年完成了这个项目，此后也一直支持两届心理学家走过他们的历程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖金以及我自己的独家支持套餐，无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组智囊会、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南-梅森的犒劳，以及限时的一对一辅导福利。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 请通过简介中链接的我的福利页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。

sentences.en: What if the thing you've been searching for your whole life isn't happiness?
sentences.zh: 如果你毕生寻找的东西其实并不是幸福，会怎么样？

sentences.en: Not success, not confidence, not motivation.
sentences.zh: 不是成功，不是自信，也不是动力。

sentences.en: What if it's safety?
sentences.zh: 如果它是安全感呢？

sentences.en: Because when humans feel truly safe, something remarkable happens.
sentences.zh: 因为当人类感到真正安全时，奇妙的事情就会发生。

sentences.en: We learn, we connect, we create, and we grow.
sentences.zh: 我们学习，我们建立连接，我们创造，我们成长。

sentences.en: And today I'm going to explore the psychology of feeling safe.
sentences.zh: 今天我将探讨安全感的心理学。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Welcome to Inner Work.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到“内修”。

sentences.en: In the main episode of Psychology Actually, I was talking with Dr. Mia Hobbs and Dr. Paula Redmond about knitting.
sentences.zh: 在《实际上是心理学》的主节目中，我曾和米娅·霍布斯博士以及保拉·雷德蒙德博士谈论过织毛衣的话题。

sentences.en: And one of the things that came up was the idea of safety, really.
sentences.zh: 其中谈到的一点，其实就是安全感的概念。

sentences.en: And how it seemed to give them those moments of deep exhale to be knitting and engaged in that in a way which just lights them up and helps them to relax.
sentences.zh: 以及织毛衣并沉浸其中似乎能给他们带来那些深深叹息的时刻，这种方式能点亮他们并帮助他们放松。

sentences.en: In a way that nothing else seems to do.
sentences.zh: 以一种其他任何事情似乎都做不到的方式。

sentences.en: And this idea of safety and the psychology of safety is one that I keep coming back to and tripping over lately.
sentences.zh: 安全感的这个概念以及安全感心理学是我最近不断回想并频频深思的一个话题。

sentences.en: I'd love to know, how would you know if you felt safe?
sentences.zh: 我很想知道，你怎么才能知道自己是否有安全感？

sentences.en: When did you last feel safe?
sentences.zh: 你上一次感到安全是什么时候？

sentences.en: How would you know what that would look like?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: So let's take a little look at what safety is.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看安全感究竟是什么。

sentences.en: I think firstly, it might be helpful to look at it being an absence of something.
sentences.zh: 我想首先，看看它作为某种事物的缺失可能会很有帮助。

sentences.en: So that's no danger, no threat, no risk.
sentences.zh: 也就是没有危险，没有威胁，没有风险。

sentences.en: And often when I'm with people and we kind of do achieve that sense of safety, you do notice those deep exhale moments.
sentences.zh: 通常，当我与人们在一起并且我们确实获得了那种安全感时，你会注意到那些深深叹息的时刻。

sentences.en: And it's a really physiological shift when you have that.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有那种感觉时，这是一种真正的生理转变。

sentences.en: I hope you are regularly experiencing moments of safety, if not, you know, periods and chunks of feeling safe and loved and contained.
sentences.zh: 我希望你经常能体验到安全的时刻，如果没有，你知道的，也希望有那种感到安全、被爱和被包容的时期和阶段。

sentences.en: But what I know is that that is not the case for lots of people.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，对很多人来说并非如此。

sentences.en: Lots of people, because of the way they've been raised or because of the relationships they found themselves in as a result of friendships or intimate partner relationships,
sentences.zh: 许多人，由于他们的成长方式，或者由于友谊或亲密伴侣关系而陷入的人际关系中，

sentences.en: will be constantly kind of scanning for criticism, constantly on edge and expecting things to be, you know, problematic and chaotic soon.
sentences.zh: 会不断地寻找批评的迹象，时刻处于边缘状态，并期望事情很快就会出现问题和陷入混乱。

sentences.en: And so sometimes even when somebody's feeling safe, that can feel really threatening in itself because their whole kind of body, mind and soul, if you like,
sentences.zh: 因此，有时即使某人感到安全，这本身也可能让人感到极具威胁，因为他们的整个身心和灵魂，如果你愿意这么说的话，

sentences.en: is constantly scanning for that threat and thinking it's all going to go to pot any minute now.
sentences.zh: 一直在扫描这种威胁，并认为随时都可能一团糟。

sentences.en: So, you know, abort, abort, get safe, get safe.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，中止，中止，找安全，找安全。

sentences.en: Because actually their nervous system has been raised and schooled on chaos and unpredictability.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上他们的神经系统是在混乱和不可预测的环境中长大和被塑造的。

sentences.en: So when things feel consistent and calm and kind of like plodding along or like your needs are being met, that can feel threatening in itself.
sentences.zh: 所以当事情感觉持续、平静、按部就班或者像你的需求得到满足时，这本身就会让人感到具有威胁。

sentences.en: And as a result, there might be some kind of self-sabotage behaviour.
sentences.zh: 因此，可能会出现某种自我破坏的行为。

sentences.en: So ending a relationship or, you know, doing something a little bit more chaotic or or finding fault in situations where there might not actually be any fault.
sentences.zh: 比如结束一段关系，或者做一些更混乱的事情，或者在实际上可能没有任何错误的情况下在情况中挑毛病。

sentences.en: And, you know, just kind of blowing up our lives a little bit.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，就是把我们的生活搞得有点一团糟。

sentences.en: So I would invite you, if you're watching this, to reflect on what behaviours crop up for you when you feel safe.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你正在看这个，我想请你反思一下，当你感到安全时，会出现什么行为？

sentences.en: Are they always adaptive, which would be leaning in, taking those breaths, enjoying those moments?
sentences.zh: 它们总是适应性的吗，比如融入其中、做那些深呼吸、享受那些时刻？

sentences.en: Or do they sometimes look a little bit different?
sentences.zh: 还是有时看起来有点不同？

sentences.en: What happens when we're not feeling safe is that we will likely strive all the harder.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到没有安全感时，发生的情况是我们可能会更加努力地奋斗。

sentences.en: We might overwork.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会过度工作。

sentences.en: We might outperform people or want to.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会超越别人，或者想要超越别人。

sentences.en: We might mask our true feelings.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会掩饰自己的真实感受。

sentences.en: We might push people away.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会把人推开。

sentences.en: We might people please.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会讨好别人。

sentences.en: Or we might just generally feel like we are burning out or that we're not truly being seen for who we are.
sentences.zh: 或者我们可能普遍觉得自己在筋疲力尽，或者我们没有被真正看到我们是谁。

sentences.en: But none of that feels very gratifying and, you know, none of it is sustainable in the medium to long term.
sentences.zh: 但这些感觉都不是很有满足感，而且，你知道的，从中长期来看，这些都是不可持续的。

sentences.en: People find safety in a variety of ways.
sentences.zh: 人们通过各种各样的方式寻找安全感。

sentences.en: So it might be that, you know, like Mia, like Paula, you're finding it in knitting or something crafty.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，可能就像米娅、保拉一样，你在织毛衣或某种手工中找到它。

sentences.en: When I haven't got a broken hand, I like a little bit of calligraphy every now and then.
sentences.zh: 当我手没受伤的时候，我偶尔也喜欢练一点书法。

sentences.en: I like swimming.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢游泳。

sentences.en: I like walking.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢散步。

sentences.en: I love cuddles with my children.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢和我的孩子们拥抱。

sentences.en: My youngest one is especially snuggly.
sentences.zh: 我的小儿子特别喜欢依偎。

sentences.en: And, you know, as I'm recording this, he's about to turn 10 and he promises me he will always remain snuggly.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当我录制这个节目时，他快要10岁了，他向我保证他会一直这么喜欢依偎。

sentences.en: But, you know, probably he won't.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，他大概不会。

sentences.en: I'm going to need to look to get my snuggles in elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 我得去别的地方找地方求抱抱了。

sentences.en: So I will drop a memo to the husband that more hugs are going to be required.
sentences.zh: 所以我要给丈夫留个便条，说明以后需要更多的拥抱。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here for Inner Work.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家收看“内修”。

sentences.en: I would love any feedback you have.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意听取你的任何反馈。

sentences.en: This is a pretty new show.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当新的节目。

sentences.en: So I would love to know that it's hitting the spot.
sentences.zh: 所以我很想知道它是否切中要害。

sentences.en: The next episode of Inner Work will be available wherever you get your podcasts and on YouTube from 8 p.m.
sentences.zh: 下一期“内修”节目将在英国时间晚上8点开始在各大播客平台和YouTube上播出。

sentences.en: UK time.
sentences.zh: 英国时间。

sentences.en: And then Psychology Actually, as you might know already, is available on Saturdays from 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 然后正如你可能已经知道的那样，《实际上是心理学》于周六上午10点在YouTube上发布，并从周一上午6点起在各大播客平台发布。

sentences.en: on YouTube and wherever you get your podcasts from 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 在各大播客平台从早上6点开始。

sentences.en: on Monday.
sentences.zh: 在周一。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。
